NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A in the Upstate: what Greenville NDT technicians and suppliers should check

Greenville's aerospace work centers on Donaldson Field at the SC Technology & Aviation Center, which the Upstate SC Alliance describes as the global home of Lockheed Martin's F-16 production and sustainment operations. Lockheed's Greenville site also carries out modification, depot-level maintenance, mid-life upgrades and parts fabrication for military and civil aircraft. Across town, GE Vernova builds large gas turbines for power plants. Both businesses buy castings, forgings and machined parts from the same regional supply base, yet the NDT behind their hardware can sit under different personnel standards. The general comparison is in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.

A power turbine is not an aero engine

A gas turbine built for a generating station is industrial equipment. Its inspection is governed by the manufacturer's specifications and by ASME and AWS requirements, and the industrial inspection firms that serve power generation usually certify their people under written practices built on SNT-TC-1A, or occasionally CP-189. Duke Energy's Oconee station near Seneca and other plants in the Carolinas add outage work of the same kind.

Flight hardware follows a different chain. Suppliers to airframe and engine makers usually find NAS 410, or EN 4179 on European programs, in the purchase-order quality clause, and on defense programs NAS 410 is the successor to MIL-STD-410. An Upstate foundry or forge that ships to both markets can therefore end up certifying the same penetrant inspector twice, under two written practices, with two sets of records behind them.

The fighter line and the shops that feed it

F-16 production brings sheet-metal, machining, coating and special process work into the region. Lockheed's own inspectors certify under the company's written practice, so the honest way to learn which document governs there is to ask its Level 3 which standard and revision that practice names. Suppliers feeding the line generally meet the requirement in the buyer's quality clause and, where they hold Nadcap NDT accreditation, have their personnel files checked against AC7114. Methods on that work lean toward penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing of machined, cast and forged parts; see penetrant testing of castings and ultrasonic testing of castings and forgings.

Checklist before you switch from tires, autos or power to aerospace

  1. Ask which standard and revision the written practice certifies to, and who holds the Responsible Level 3 (RL3) designation.
  2. Bring course records showing the outline, the instructor and the hours for each method. A bare attendance slip gives an RL3 nothing to credit.
  3. Bring a signed experience log split by method. Hours earned at a tire plant or a turbine shop still count as experience; the RL3 decides how much.
  4. Plan for extra formal penetrant and magnetic particle training, because NAS 410 asks for more documented training in the surface methods than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  5. Keep your near-vision and color records current. Neither scheme lets an inspector sign results on a lapsed vision examination.

An SNT-TC-1A certificate on its own does not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement, and neither scheme travels between employers. The evidence behind your certificate is what travels.

For Upstate quality managers

If one plant takes aerospace orders alongside power or automotive work, run two clearly separate programs or two clearly separate sections of one written practice. Print the governing standard and revision on every certification. NAS 410 Revision 6 was released in December 2025; move to it on your customers' timetable and update the training material and examination banks in the same step. Expect Nadcap and customer auditors to sample inspectors and follow each one to the training, experience, examination and vision evidence. Atlantis prepares and reviews NAS 410 audit documentation for your RL3 to approve, and our aerospace audit support helps get written practices, procedures and examination records ready before the auditor arrives.

How Atlantis helps in Greenville

Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Theory is online and self-paced, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions; practice happens in the Practical NDT simulator; the hands-on work and practical examination take place at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Greenville. The aerospace NDT training page shows how that route serves aircraft and engine work, and our ASNT Level III consulting writes aerospace written practices on SNT-TC-1A aligned to the customer's flow-down and Nadcap AC7114. Upstate plants that need inspection can call on Atlantis for UT, MT, PT and VT.

Stated plainly for the Upstate: Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3. If you want SNT-TC-1A-based hours credited toward a NAS 410 certification, the employer's RL3 makes that call, and you should ask before enrolling.
